body:
This reproduces on the main branch. FWIW, here's the relevant part of the backtrace:

<details>
<summary>Click to expand/collapse</summary>

```
Thread 1 "python" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
0x00007fffc49d8e04 in at::native::<lambda()>::<lambda()>::operator() (
    __closure=<optimized out>, __closure=<optimized out>)
    at /work2/kurtamohler/development/pytorch-1/aten/src/ATen/native/EmbeddingBag.cpp:798
798	  AT_DISPATCH_INDEX_TYPES(offsets.scalar_type(), "_embedding_bag_cpu_impl", [&]() {
(gdb) bt
#0  0x00007fffc49d8e04 in at::native::<lambda()>::<lambda()>::operator() (
    __closure=<optimized out>, __closure=<optimized out>)
    at /work2/kurtamohler/development/pytorch-1/aten/src/ATen/native/EmbeddingBag.cpp:798
#1  at::native::<lambda()>::operator() (__closure=<optimized out>, __closure=<optimized out>)
    at /work2/kurtamohler/development/pytorch-1/aten/src/ATen/native/EmbeddingBag.cpp:798
#2  at::native::check_arguments(at::Tensor const&, at::Tensor const&, at::Tensor const&, long, c10::optional<at::Tensor> const&, bool) ()
    at /work2/kurtamohler/development/pytorch-1/aten/src/ATen/native/EmbeddingBag.cpp:798
#3  0x00007fffc49edff3 in at::native::_embedding_bag_cpu_impl(at::Tensor const&, at::Tensor const&, at::Tensor const&, long, at::Tensor const&, bool, long, bool) ()
    at /home/kurtamohler/.conda/envs/pytorch-1/x86_64-conda-linux-gnu/include/c++/9.5.0/bits/atomic_base.h:539
#4  0x00007fffc49ee485 in at::native::_embedding_bag_forward_only_cpu(at::Tensor const&, at::Tensor const&, at::Tensor const&, bool, long, bool, c10::optional<at::Tensor> const&, bool, long) ()
    at /work2/kurtamohler/development/pytorch-1/aten/src/ATen/native/EmbeddingBag.cpp:1156

```

</details>

`offsets` is supposed to either be `None` or have only one dimension, according to the docs [here](https://pytorch.org/docs/master/generated/torch.nn.functional.embedding_bag.html?highlight=embedding_bag#torch.nn.functional.embedding_bag). Also, `input` is supposed to only be 1D or 2D. So these cases should be throwing errors about invalid argument shapes.

The reason this causes a segfault is that, since `offsets` is assumed to be 1D if it is not `None`, before it checks that the values in `offsets` are correct, it checks `offsets.size(0) > 0` to avoid trying to access invalid memory. But in this case, `offsets.size(0)` is greater than 0, but `offsets.numel()` is 0 since there are zeros in the higher dimensions of `offsets.shape`.

I'll add the shape checks.

Some relevant details:

`torch.nn.functional.embedding_bag` already performs the dimensionality checks here: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/77f1f98479b204b2d0151d9cf3700f99915b9d50/torch/nn/functional.py#L2334-L2357

`torch.nn.functional.embedding_bag` ends up calling `torch.embedding_bag`. `torch.embedding_bag` is not in the documentation, and it's not being called anywhere else, aside from a benchmark test in `benchmarks/static_runtime/test_static_runtime.cc`. It seems like users aren't really supposed to use it, and they should use `torch.nn.functional.embedding_bag` instead.

Since `torch._embedding_bag` and `torch._embedding_bag_forward_only` begin with underscores, users aren't supposed to call it. And they are only called within `at::embedding_bag` here: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/77f1f98479b204b2d0151d9cf3700f99915b9d50/aten/src/ATen/native/EmbeddingBag.cpp#L1123-L1131

It would be nice to refactor this stuff to be a bit simpler. We might be able to move the whole definition of `torch.nn.functional.embedding_bag` to C++. But I imagine there would be some backward compatibility issues with that. And I don't know the reasons why things are set up this way, so maybe refactoring wouldn't be a good idea anyway.

So for now, I guess the best solution is still to just duplicate dimensionality checks into `at::_embedding_bag_forward_only` and `at::_embedding_bag`. Since `at::embedding_bag` just calls into one of those, it will pick up the checks as well. The checks aren't expensive anyway, so duplication shouldn't noticeably change performance

issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

A test for `torch.nn.functional.embedding_bag` triggers "IOT instruction (core dumpd)" error.
### Test
```python
import torch

self = torch.tensor([2, 4, 8, 8, 7, 3, 1, 8, 7, 8, 1, 1, 0, 0, 3, 1, 0, 2, 1, 5, 8, 7, 9, 7, 0, 0, 7, 6, 5, 5, 9, 1, 6, 2, 9, 1, 4, 3, 2, 3, 1, 1, 0, 6, 3, 9, 3, 9, 6, 6, 9, 2, 8, 5, 7])
weight = torch.rand([100, 5], dtype=torch.float32)
offsets = torch.tensor([0,  6, 12, 15, 25, 32, 40, 42, 46, 53, 53])

res = torch.nn.functional.embedding_bag(
    self, weight, offsets,
    norm_type = 2.0,
    scale_grad_by_freq = False,
    mode = 'mean',
    sparse = True,
    include_last_offset = True,
    padding_idx = 61
)
```
### Error Log
(The error message is non-deterministic, sometimes it also reports `free(): invalid next size (normal)` 
```
double free or corruption (!prev)
[1]    260353 IOT instruction (core dumped)
```
